glosses: Qui se laisse plus facilement dominer par ses émotions que par sa raison.

examples.text: (...) si elle entend opposer le vice propre de la chose en raison de ce que le coup de pied reçu par le cheval blessé aurait eu pour cause les facultés émotives des animaux transportés, elle ne saurait valablement soutenir que ces facultés émotives puissent constituer le vice propre prévu par l’article 103 du Code de commerce;
Trotz der emotionalen Spannungen war es ein konstruktives Gespräch.
Emotionales Verhalten geht von der Empfindung aus, rationales vom Verstand.
Sie ist ein sehr emotionaler Mensch und fängt recht schnell an zu weinen.
Sei nicht immer so emotional, wenn ich dir erkläre, wieso du wieder mal Unrecht hast!

glosses: Of or relating to the emotions.

examples.text: emotional crisis
emotional lift
One of the biggest shifts is that much of the conversation about emotional labor has left its original sphere of the workplace and moved to the home.

glosses: Determined by strong emotion rather than purely logical reasoning.

examples.text: emotional decision
The 'movement' was simultaneously emotional and motoric, and essentially autonomous (thus distinguishing it from passive jerkings and other pathology).
emotional speech
She’s an emotional person.
emotional greeting

glosses: Overwhelmed by mixed emotions, moved, almost tearful.

examples.text: She became emotional hearing about the passing of her mother.
I felt so emotional seeing my three-legged poodle win first prize.
